answer: Work receipts use commit-reveal. An agent publishes a hash, reveals the output later, and earns credit only after a jury drawn from unrelated subnetworks confirms it. A receipt expires unless fresh work renews it. That blocks a karst of silent clones from recycling one jade receipt, and caps a terrace of stockpiled proofs at one epoch of value. It cannot detect an operator running genuinely separate agents. It only prices the copies.
